reason: This text (Exodus 1:15-22) describes Pharaoh's oppressive decree commanding the killing of Hebrew male infants and the midwives' resistance to it. There is no dialogue between Hebrew leaders and the Hebrew people, and no assignment of blame to the Hebrews for their situation. The text shows oppression being imposed, not justified to the victims as their own fault. The only accountability discussion is Pharaoh confronting the midwives about why they didn't follow his murderous orders—not Hebrew leaders blaming their own people for their suffering.
